authorship: Curator arithmetic illustrations; not author code

relative_threshold.locator: Section 3 and Section 4 Equation (1), printed p. 57 / PDF p. 2
relative_threshold.interpretation: Multiplying a negative maximum log score by a ratio below one would remove every item under the printed non-strict discard rule. Applying that ratio to probabilities is different and keeps the best item in this example. The paper needs an explicit score-domain interpretation; this calculation does not establish which domain the authors implemented.

predicted_length_is_not_a_maximum.locator: Section 5.2 Equation (13) and Section 6.1, printed pp. 3057–3058 / PDF pp. 4–5
predicted_length_is_not_a_maximum.interpretation: Using predicted length as R would certify stopping here, yet an allowed longer completion can beat the incumbent despite lower raw log probability. If the decoder truly enforces R as its maximum permitted length, that longer completion is excluded and this example does not contradict the bound.

limitations: Arithmetic examples only; no author implementation, trained model, benchmark or full decoder was run.
The relative-score calculation demonstrates a domain ambiguity, not a verified author bug or correction.
The BP-Norm calculation concerns a forecast used without a genuine length cap; the valid maximum-length theorem is not challenged.
Numerical values are illustrative curator inputs, not reported measurements.
